title: Lifting a bounded-above acyclic complex through an ideal
statement: Let $R$ be a ring, let $I \subset R$ be an ideal, and let $\mathcal{P}$ be a class of $R$-modules. Assume: (1) every $P \in \mathcal{P}$ is projective; (2) if $P_1 \in \mathcal{P}$ and $P_1 \oplus P_2 \in \mathcal{P}$, then $P_2 \in \mathcal{P}$; and (3) every map $P_1 \to P_2$ between members of $\mathcal{P}$ that is surjective modulo $I$ is surjective. If $E^\bullet$ is a bounded-above acyclic complex of $R/I$-modules [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] whose terms are each isomorphic to $P/IP$ for some $P \in \mathcal{P}$, then there exists a bounded-above acyclic complex $A^\bullet$ with all terms in $\mathcal{P}$ and an isomorphism $A^\bullet/IA^\bullet \cong E^\bullet$ of complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules].

proof.text: Construct the zero complex using the one-point module. The summand condition implies that it belongs to the class and that the class is closed under isomorphism. The zero comparison is an isomorphism above b. This initializes a finite tail at b+1.

Apply the one-degree extension lemma recursively, at left endpoints b+1-n for natural n. Keep the extension maps and their commuting reduction comparisons, giving a sequential diagram of complexes. Each term and differential stabilizes once its degree lies in the constructed tail.

Take the degreewise colimit of the sequential diagram. Mathlib eventual-constancy identifies each colimit term with a tail term, so it belongs to the class and is zero above b. For each degree choose a stage containing it and both adjacent degrees: the induced short-complex isomorphism transfers exactness. The compatible comparisons descend through the extension-of-scalars image of the colimit. Their components and the stabilized colimit inclusions are isomorphisms; hence the descended comparison is an isomorphism of complexes. All this assembly is proved directly in Lean, with no additional proof gaps.

lean.statement: theorem exists_acyclic_lift_mod_ideal (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (P : ModuleCat.{max u v} R → Prop) (hprojective : ∀ M, P M → Projective M) (hsummand : ∀ M₁ M₂ M₁₂ : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, P M₁ → P M₁₂ → Nonempty (M₁₂ ≅ ModuleCat.of R (M₁ × M₂)) → P M₂) (hsurjective : ∀ (M₁ M₂ : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (f : M₁ ⟶ M₂), P M₁ → P M₂ → Function.Surjective ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).map f) → Function.Surjective f) (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} (R ⧸ I)) ℤ) (hbounded : ∃ b : ℤ, E.IsStrictlyLE b) (hacyclic : E.Acyclic) (hterms : ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, P M ∧ Nonempty ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).obj M ≅ E.X i)) : ∃ A : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ, (∃ b : ℤ, A.IsStrictlyLE b) ∧ A.Acyclic ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, P (A.X i)) ∧ Nonempty (((ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj A ≅ E)
